model: Claude, via the artifact runtime's sample capability (images)
how: The console sends the current CAM_FRONT and CAM_BACK frames to Claude and streams back a scene description. A real vision-language model running on real frames, on the viewer's own Claude account.
why_not_blip: scripts/vlm_scene_understanding.py targets Salesforce BLIP. huggingface.co returns 403 at the egress proxy from the cloud container AND from the local machine, with no cached copy on either -- an organisation policy denial, not a missing dependency. Rather than ship a dead panel or fabricate captions, the VLM slot is served by a model this environment can actually reach.
honest_difference: This is NOT the repo's BLIP pipeline and does not share its weights or its latency. It is a different, larger VLM, called at view time, and no metric in this project depends on its output.
caveats: Requires the viewer to allow the call; it spends their Claude usage.
Descriptions are qualitative. Nothing downstream consumes them.
BLIP remains the code path in the repo for an environment that can reach the model hub.
